params.body:
## What

Two things the new run record made visible on 2026-09-20.

**Instagram asked Apify on every round.** `tiktok-trends` rests twenty hours, `instagram-search` had no cadence. The collector runs every 6 to 25 minutes, so that was 57 rounds in a day, up to eight actor runs each, and nearly all of them came back with the same 71 posts (`nothing-new`). The actor charges $0.0023 a post, so a full round is about $0.16. Twice the collector cut the adapter off at 150 seconds and threw the harvest away, while Apify billed the runs all the same. The Apify headroom went from $47 to $41.21 in that day (trial runs and TikTok included).

**The record did not carry the bill.** A pay-per-event run shows `usageTotalUsd: 0` when it ends. Measured on `apify~instagram-hashtag-scraper` on 2026-09-21: still 0 after 8 seconds, 0.0069 after 16, while `chargedEventCounts` is there after about 3. Every adapter read the bill at the moment the run ended, so TikTok and the Chinese hot ranks booked (almost) zero and Instagram booked its declared guess.

## How

- `instagram-search`: `cadence: {everyHours: 6}`. The search terms come from TikTok and change once a day; four rounds a day still catch what is posted under a tag during the day. The collector's existing rule applies: it rests only after a round that did its work, and tries again next round after a failure.
- A ceiling of $0.05 on every run (ten posts cost about $0.023), tried on the box: accepted by the actor.
- Its own clock: past 110 seconds it starts no new term, keeps what it has and logs which terms it did not get to, so it finishes before the collector's 150-second cap.
- `apify.mjs`: `chargeOf(run)` takes the larger of the settled total and the counted events times the actor's own price per event (tiered prices are left alone, a guessed tier is not a bill). `settledCostUsd(runIds)` waits three seconds once, reads every run once, and returns `null` rather than a false zero when nothing could be read, so the record falls back on the declared price.
- All three Apify adapters collect their run ids, failed runs included (a failed run is still billed), and book the settled bill.
- `test/apify-bill.test.mjs` pins the arithmetic, the null, the cadence, and that no Apify adapter reads `run.usageUsd` at the end of a run any more.

## After the merge

The next Instagram round books a `cost_usd` near $0.16 instead of the flat $0.20, and then no Instagram row appears for six hours. `china-hotrank` rows start carrying what the six runs really cost.
params.title: Instagram search rests six hours, and the record carries the bill Apify settled
